_comment: Flux v8 spec for the LIVE Quip faucet, which serves the AGLAIS chain.
Starting point for the dashboard wizard ONLY — the canonical spec is always the export.
🔴🔴 CORRECTED 2026-09-07 (QUI-1225). THIS FILE USED TO DESCRIBE A SECOND, PARALLEL APP
CALLED `quipfaucetaglais`. That plan was superseded and the app was NEVER REGISTERED; the
existing `quipfaucet` subscription was repointed at aglais instead. Following the old version
of this file would have registered a SECOND faucet on the SAME funder mnemonic — two
processes, one base wallet, two in-memory nonce lanes — which is exactly the QUI-723/831
stranded-future-nonce failure, aimed at the live faucet. Hence `instances: 1` below is
correctness, not cost, and hence there must be exactly one of these apps.
Evidence, all from the public Flux API and DNS on 2026-09-07:
/apps/location/quipfaucetaglais  -> data: []                (never deployed)
/apps/location/quipfaucet        -> 1 instance, running since 2026-08-28
dig faucet.aglais.quip.network   -> CNAME quipfaucet.app.runonflux.io
dig faucet.testnet.quip.network  -> NXDOMAIN                (old chain's name is gone)
/apps/appspecifications/quipfaucet -> geolocation [acEU, acNA, a!cEU_RU], i.e. the aglais
geolocation, not the old testnet's [a!cEU_RU]; expire 114846 at height 2917711,
so the subscription ran to roughly 2026-10-13. Since renewed: checked 2026-10-14,
expire 103003 at height 3017562, i.e. block 3120565, roughly 2026-11-12.
⚠ The live spec itself cannot be read back — Enterprise apps return `compose: []` to the
public API. Confirm against the dashboard export before submitting anything.
UNCHANGED and deliberate: ports/containerPorts 8087, containerData /data, cpu 1 /
ram 2048 / hdd 1, instances 1, staticip false, repoauth "" (the registry is public),
geolocation [acEU, acNA, a!cEU_RU]. The funder key is NOT unchanged: see RUNTIME 119 below.
QUI-1225 — TELEMETRY. The faucet now ships its own logs to observe.quip.network over OTLP,
so the record of every mint outlives the Flux console (which is wiped on every update, not
only on relocation, and cannot be backfilled). The endpoint and service name are BAKED INTO
THE IMAGE — see the Dockerfile for why — so the only new variable here is the secret,
taking this component from 2 to 3 of the 20 allowed. It is safe in this spec only because
the app is Enterprise; on a non-Enterprise app the Flux public API serves it in the clear.
⚠ Telemetry is off unless the key is present, so omitting it degrades to today's behaviour
rather than failing. DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 switches it off without a rebuild.
⚠ The repotag below is a placeholder. RUNTIME 119 (the spec-119 relaunch) needs a new build
from relaunch/spec119-faucet: !21's direct mint, pinned to quip-validator v0.4.0. CI builds
images only on main and on tags, so tag the pushed commit (not v-prefixed: faucet-119-rc1).
There is NO rollback image on 119: every earlier image mints through Sudo::sudo(FaucetOps.mint),
which runtime 119 rejects. The image live before the relaunch (per the 2026-09-07 deploy),
registry.gitlab.com/quip.network/faucet:qui1225-rc1-amd64
@sha256:d5ae5dcfa439deab659def08d1ddf84d0de4b4b21cbe9e01679c27e6ebb3db55,
is a rollback target for aglais 118 only.
⭐ RUNTIME 119 AUTHORITY MODEL. The faucet mints with FaucetOps.mint, signed by the FaucetOps
authority that the Foundation appoints with a 2-of-3 setAuthority motion, not by sudo. At
genesis the authority is op-1, which is also sudo: the faucet must NOT run on op-1's key.
Relaunch order: before the switch, stop the legacy faucet and take op-1's key off the host
(launch plan T0 step 5). Then fund F, pass setAuthority(F), wait until that block is
FINALIZED, and update this app with F's mnemonic and the new repotag in ONE Soft Reinstall,
replacing the prefilled op-1 value. Any earlier and the faucet crash-loops on
'configured funder is not FaucetOps.Authority'. Check the boot line reads
'funder: <F> (key from QUIP_FAUCET_FAUCET_KEY)'.
Take F's AccountId for the motion from the binary's own 'funder: <ss58>' line: H4 hybrid
accounts differ from what other tools derive from the same mnemonic.
Startup checks run at the finalized head and fail CLOSED: runtime exactly 119 / tx 7,
FaucetOps.Authority == this funder, state Enabled, budget remaining. They are also what aims
this app now: on any other chain the runtime or authority check refuses to start.
⚠ Every later runtime upgrade (setCode) needs a rebuilt faucet deployed with it: the exact
119/7 check answers 503 from the upgrade block until the new image is live.
⚠ `--allow-any-chain` only disables verify_dev_chain(), the dev-chain name check; production
has to set it.
⚠ `--max-amount-plancks=11000000000000` raises the per-request cap from one dispense (10 AGLS)
to 11 AGLS, so the status.sh health check's 11 AGLS verification drip still gets through.
BEFORE DEPLOYING:
1. repotag digest — build + push, then pin `repo:TAG@sha256:DIGEST`. A bare `repo@sha256:`
is REJECTED by Flux.
2. Enterprise ON — QUIP_FAUCET_FAUCET_KEY is F's mnemonic (the faucet authority); empty `enterprise` ships
it as PLAINTEXT env. The toggle generates the blob at submit; it is not a pasted value.
3. Create the faucet.aglais.quip.network CNAME to the new app's FDM name once registered.
TLS is terminated by Flux FDM at the custom domain — there is no certifier/Tarsnap leg
here, unlike the bootnodes.
4. No environmentParameters value may be empty — Flux rejects the whole submission.
So omit ONEUPTIME_TELEMETRY_KEY entirely rather than leaving it blank.
5. This is an UPDATE to the existing quipfaucet app, not a new registration. Land the
repotag bump and F's key in ONE submit, after setAuthority(F) is finalized: an env change needs a Soft Reinstall,
not a Restart, and at instances:1 each one is a real outage of the public faucet.
REPLACE every <REPLACE:...> before use.
name: quipfaucet
description: Quip aglais testnet faucet: native (SS58 / 0x+64-hex) and EVM (0x+40-hex) funding

compose.name: faucet
compose.description: Rust quip-faucet for runtime 119. Funder is the FaucetOps authority F; it mints into a dedicated base wallet with FaucetOps.mint, funds the /sign pool, and serves /request, /sign, /health over plain HTTP. TLS is terminated by Flux FDM.
compose.repotag: <REPLACE:registry.gitlab.com/quip.network/faucet:TAG-amd64@sha256:DIGEST — rebuild required, the OTLP exporter is compiled in. A bare repo@sha256: is REJECTED by Flux>
environmentParameters: QUIP_FAUCET_FAUCET_KEY=<REPLACE:F's mnemonic, the FaucetOps authority appointed by the Foundation motion. NEVER op-1 (op-1 is sudo). Only after setAuthority(F) is finalized>

ONEUPTIME_TELEMETRY_KEY=<REPLACE:Telemetry Ingestion Key UUID from the OneUptime dashboard — project settings, Telemetry Ingestion Keys. Omit this line entirely to ship without telemetry; do NOT leave it blank>

enterprise: <REPLACE:NOT a value you paste — flip the Enterprise toggle in the wizard's General tab, which generates the blob at submit. Leaving this off ships F's mnemonic (the faucet authority) as PLAINTEXT env>
